title: Bot personality variants — visual differentiation + random in solo
notes: S100 introduced three bot personalities (hunter / coward / miner) but visually every bot still uses the same 'rose' palette + no accessory marker — the player can't tell them apart at a glance. This sprint wires personality to the procedural recipe so each variant has its own look.

User request also asks: when running solo with no ?botPersonality= URL param, pick a RANDOM personality per page load (stable across round restarts of the same match). Pre-fix the default was always 'hunter', so every solo session played the same.

Mapping: hunter → ember palette + antennae accessory (aggressive scout); coward → slate palette + visor accessory (defensive); miner → sand palette + cap accessory (workman). Three palettes chosen from the existing BomberPalettes for instant visual readability.

stories.title: Solo default: pick a random bot personality per page load
stories.summary: examples/kaboom-crew/src/difficulty.ts — extend readBotPersonalityFromUrl with a `pickRandomBotPersonality(rng?: () => number)` helper that returns one of hunter/coward/miner with equal probability. Read flow: if the URL carries `?botPersonality=hunter|coward|miner` use that (explicit override); otherwise pick random once. The bootstrap caches the choice in a module-level singleton so all the reads (initial spawn + round restart) get the SAME personality across a single page load — the player isn't surprised by a mid-match swap.
verification: acceptance: examples/kaboom-crew/src/difficulty.ts gains pickRandomBotPersonality(rng) helper + resolveSessionBotPersonality(search, rng) which honours URL override OR returns a random pick memoised once per page load. _resetSessionBotPersonality() test escape hatch added. bootstrap.ts uses resolveSessionBotPersonality at all three call sites (initial spawn, round restart, difficulty change) so solo defaults to random per page load with stable choice across rounds.

stories.title: Unit test the random personality picker + URL override precedence
stories.summary: examples/kaboom-crew/tests/unit/difficulty.test.ts — add tests covering: (1) pickRandomBotPersonality with a deterministic stub rng returns each kind for the expected mod-3 input; (2) URL override beats the random default (any of hunter/coward/miner takes precedence); (3) absent URL param triggers the random path; (4) the bootstrap-facing 'session personality' helper memoises one pick per page load.
verification: acceptance: examples/kaboom-crew/tests/unit/difficulty.test.ts adds 5 tests — BOT_PERSONALITIES canonical list, pickRandomBotPersonality maps mod-3 rng deterministically (hunter/coward/miner), URL override beats random, empty/unknown URL triggers random path, memoisation across calls (rng invoked exactly once even with 3 calls). 10/10 difficulty tests pass.

stories.title: Recipe palette overrides per personality
stories.summary: examples/kaboom-crew/bootstrap.ts makeKaboomRecipe gains an optional personality arg. Mapping: hunter → 'ember', coward → 'slate', miner → 'sand'. Falls back to the existing 'rose' when personality is absent (e.g. on the connected profile where the server owns bot.1). Player stays on 'sky' (player.1 path is unchanged). Wiring: the two attachUi sites (initial spawn + reset) pass the cached session personality.
verification: acceptance: examples/kaboom-crew/src/kaboom-recipe.ts (new) exposes makeKaboomRecipe(ownerId, personality?) + PERSONALITY_PALETTE map. bot.1 with personality returns paletteName 'ember'/'slate'/'sand' for hunter/coward/miner; without personality falls back to legacy 'rose'. player.1 stays 'sky' regardless. bootstrap.ts swaps the inline helper for the new module-level function and passes the session personality at all 3 call sites + the renderer's resolveForOwner closure.

stories.title: Recipe builder returns the personality-mapped palette
stories.summary: examples/kaboom-crew/tests/unit/recipe-personality.test.ts — call makeKaboomRecipe('bot.1', 'hunter') / ('bot.1', 'coward') / ('bot.1', 'miner') and assert .paletteName equals 'ember' / 'slate' / 'sand' respectively. Plus: makeKaboomRecipe('bot.1') (no personality) falls back to 'rose'; makeKaboomRecipe('player.1') stays on 'sky' regardless of personality (player isn't affected).
verification: acceptance: examples/kaboom-crew/tests/unit/recipe-personality.test.ts asserts palette per personality (ember/slate/sand), backward-compat 'rose' fallback, player.1 'sky' invariance, seed-driven recipe for unknown ids. Distinctness check on PERSONALITY_PALETTE values.

stories.title: Each personality carries a distinctive accessory
stories.summary: Apply per-personality accessory override on the bot recipe: hunter → 'antennae' (head.top socket), coward → 'visor' (head.front), miner → 'cap' (head.top). Replaces whatever the seed-derived recipe picked for bot.1 so the marker is reliable regardless of seed. makeKaboomRecipe builds a single-accessory list when personality is set.
verification: acceptance: examples/kaboom-crew/src/kaboom-recipe.ts gains PERSONALITY_ACCESSORY map { hunter: 'antennae', coward: 'visor', miner: 'cap' }. bot.1 with personality always carries a single-element accessories[] holding the personality-specific kind; bot.1 without personality keeps the seed-driven accessories.

stories.title: Recipe builder writes the personality-mapped accessory
stories.summary: examples/kaboom-crew/tests/unit/recipe-personality.test.ts — assert makeKaboomRecipe('bot.1', personality).accessories[0].kind matches 'antennae' / 'visor' / 'cap' for the three personalities. Single-element list — no other accessories on the bot when personality drives the marker.
verification: acceptance: 3 of the 8 recipe-personality tests cover the accessory contract — antennae/visor/cap for hunter/coward/miner. Distinctness check on PERSONALITY_ACCESSORY values. accessories[] is single-element when personality is set.
